newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes softer ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes softer ahead of jobs data.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed much weaker on Thursday at C$1.3500 (US$0.7408) from Wednesday's close of C$1.3445 (US$0.7438) in fairly heavy trading, dealers said.
* They said a large sell order mid-afternoon by a Canadian fund manager help push the currency weaker.
* The market was tense ahead of U.S., Canada labor data expected on Friday.
The market was tense ahead of the release of non-farm payroll numbers in the United States and the January unemployment rate in Canada, dealers said.
A Reuters survey of economists is forecasting a January unemployment rate of 9.6 percent, down slightly from 9.7 percent December.

In the United States, economists polled by Reuters projected an average increase of 237,000 jobs in January non-farm payrolls against a 262,000 gain in the previous month. Any impact the data has on stocks and bonds may spill over into the Canadian dollar.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2240 marks from 1.2233 marks on Wednesday, but stayed flat at 91.65 yen.
